messages:
Noah Kim: quick heads-up, hitting a weird parity bug between Java and Kotlin SDKs when using Retrofit async + coroutine suspend wrappers. Kotlin sample app makes a single API call but server logs show two requests. attaching small repro steps.

Ella R.: can you paste the Retrofit service and how you're invoking it?

Noah Kim: service is simple:

```
interface ApiService {
  @POST("/v1/process")
  suspend fun process(@Body body: Payload): Response<Result>
}
```

Noah Kim: calling from activity: `lifecycleScope.launch { api.process(payload) }` but on some devices (Pixel 8, Android 14 emulator) the server receives duplicate POSTs ~200ms apart.

PJ: do you have any custom CallAdapterFactory or are you using Retrofit's built-in coroutine adapter?

Noah Kim: using retrofit-kotlin-coroutines-adapter from the SDK samples (we vendored a small adapter in our sdk-samples module).

Ravi: we've seen dupes when an interceptor or network layer clones the call for a retry while the original call is still in flight because of a soft socket reset. But you said both calls have identical body IDs?

Noah Kim: yes identical body id header. Server returns 200 for the first; second comes after and returns 409. client gets the 200 but UI sometimes shows a failed state because the adapter throws on the second response path?

Ella R.: hmm. Can you share OkHttp/Retrofit config? timeouts? dispatcher?

Noah Kim: OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor(tokenProvider))
  .addInterceptor(LoggingInterceptor)
  .addInterceptor(RetryInterceptor(maxRetries = 1))
  .connectTimeout(15, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .callTimeout(0, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .build()

PJ: important: suspend fun endpoints are implemented via a CallAdapter that bridges Call<T> to Deferred<T>. If your adapter mistakenly calls `call.clone().enqueue()` for some conversion, and you also have a retry interceptor that retries by cloning, you can get double-execution. Also if your adapter tries a synchronous `call.execute()` inside a background thread and the Retrofit created call was already enqueued by something else, duplicate could happen.

Ravi: another angle: converter exceptions (Moshi) thrown during response parsing can trigger the coroutine adapter to cancel and then the retry interceptor to try again. Are you seeing any parse exceptions in the stack?

Noah Kim: I saw occasional `java.io.StreamCorruptedException` in the logs on the second response. Stack: `MoshiJsonAdapter.fromJson` -> `okio.Buffer.read` -> `EOFException`. Looks like partial body on the second.

Ella R.: that suggests the first response may have been partially read and then something triggered a follow-up request that got the remainder or a truncated payload. Do you have `RetryInterceptor` aggressively retrying on any IOException?

Noah Kim: yes RetryInterceptor retries on any IOException except SSL and some whitelisted ones.

PJ: recommended changes: 1) Make CallAdapter idempotent: ensure adapter uses the same Call instance and does not enqueue/execute more than once. 2) Update RetryInterceptor to avoid retrying when the original call has already started reading the response body (i.e., only retry on specific socket-level IOExceptions and not on EOF/StreamCorrupted). 3) Consider using `callTimeout` to fail fast instead of silent retries for ambiguous network failures.

Ravi: also confirm interceptor ordering: AuthInterceptor should be an application interceptor (adds headers) and RetryInterceptor should be a network interceptor or early in the chain so it can see low-level IOExceptions. Application interceptors re-run for each retry; network interceptors are tied to a specific connection-phase. ordering matters for cloning semantics.

Noah Kim: interesting. In our SDK we register interceptors in this order: Logging (app), Auth (app), Retry (app). Should we move Retry to network interceptors?

PJ: try: client.networkInterceptors().add(RetryInterceptor) or use `addNetworkInterceptor`. That attaches it to a specific real network call and reduces retries that duplicate already-started application-level processing like body serialization. Caveat: network interceptors can't short-circuit some application-level behavior, so test thoroughly.

Ella R.: small repro I used to validate: instrument the CallAdapter to log when `call.enqueue` / `call.execute` / `call.clone()` are invoked. For suspend adapter you should see exactly one `enqueue` per logical request. If you see clone() twice, that's a bug.

Noah Kim: I added logs and found adapter enqueued once, but RetryInterceptor cloned the call and enqueued a second. Retry cloned because the original threw EOFException while reading response body. So it's a retry-on-EOF + adapter expecting a fresh body causing Moshi failure.

Ravi: change RetryInterceptor policy: don't retry on EOFException while response code is 2xx. If server returned partial body due to socket reset, retry is OK but you must ensure response body is fully consumed or closed before retrying. Also add idempotency check for POSTs: by default don't retry non-idempotent methods unless safe to do so (upload idempotency token).

PJ: final SDK guidance we should document: - sample adapters must not clone calls unnecessarily - RetryInterceptor should be conservative for non-idempotent calls - provide example TokenProvider + backoff that behaves the same in Java and Kotlin - include emulator tests for Pixel 8 Android 14 and a flaky network harness that injects EOF/socket resets.

Noah Kim: created ticket SDK-4092, PR opened with changes: 1) RetryInterceptor refined to skip EOF retries for 2xx responses and non-idempotent methods, 2) moved RetryInterceptor into network interceptors in sample app, 3) added instrumentation to the coroutine CallAdapter to guard against inadvertent clones, 4) added repro in samples/pixel8-flaky-network/ with adb scripts.

ci-bot: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/android-sdk/pull/1024 checks queued.

Ella R.: :tada: This matches our internal parity doc. Once CI passes please update the SDK migration note about interceptor ordering and calladapter semantics.

Noah Kim: will do. thanks for the triage and pointers. will post back with CI results and customer validation.

PJ: small nit: also add a note about `OkHttpClient.dispatcher().maxRequestsPerHost` in the migration doc; on older devices default values can cause queued calls to start later and interact badly with retries.

Noah Kim: noted. closing the loop after we verify in the field.
